clue.text: Stale humour starts to corrupt old and basic part of the ear

parts.note: corn is old, tired, trite humour

indicators.note: the starts of the following words means only their opening letters are kept

parts.note: opening letters of the two words
its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone complains that hackneyed jokes are spoiling the old and fundamental anatomy of the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the selected words but gives no letter; 'basic part of the ear' looks like the definition, but 'basic' supplies a letter and 'ear' is an ear of corn, not the organ of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A corncob is the central woody core of a maize ear, on which the kernels grow.

clue.text: Head of union avoiding hint about excellent nurse

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps another
avoiding means keeping clear of, so that letter is left out

parts.note: a clue is a hint

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: Head of union: its first letter
rad is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A union leader sidesteps a hint about a superb nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' is a verb here, to hold a baby tenderly; RAD is slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: To cradle is to hold gently in the arms, as one nurses a baby.

clue.text: Gag involving university in alteration of image

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to gag is to retch
OU is the Open University, Britain's distance-learning university

explanation.surface: A joke about a university featured in a doctored photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like a joke but is the verb meaning to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: A retouch is a small improvement or correction made to a photograph or painting.

clue.text: Excellent American expert probing Egyptian language

indicators.note: probing means poking inside, so one word sits within another

parts.note: Coptic is the language of Egypt's Christian church
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A top US scholar investigating an ancient Egyptian tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' belongs to the definition: the word is US slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Copacetic is American slang meaning fine, satisfactory or excellent.

clue.text: Difficult situation after quantity of fabric found in concealed location

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other

parts.note: a bolt is a roll of cloth
to be in a hole is to be in trouble

explanation.surface: A tricky spot arises after a roll of cloth turns up in a hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolt-hole is a secret refuge where one can hide away.

clue.text: Dismissive comment about promotional material in songs

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: 'Balls!' is a rude British retort meaning nonsense
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A scornful remark about the advertising that turns up inside songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls!' is crude British slang for 'rubbish!'; the dismissive word wraps the advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballads are narrative songs, so the plural noun matches the plural definition.

clue.text: Hinder eating most of the fruit biscuit

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to bar is to hinder or obstruct

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short
an olive is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone is stopped from munching nearly all of the fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims only 'the', not the fruit. A Bath Oliver is a plain, hard British cracker, invented by Dr William Oliver of Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bath Oliver is an unsweetened dry biscuit often eaten with cheese.

clue.text: Very quick, missing fine story-telling

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: flying means extremely fast
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A rapid narrator who lacks finesse.
explanation.walkthrough: F is taken from FLYING. 'Story-telling' is the informal sense of telling stories, i.e. fibbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling stories is a euphemism for telling untruths, so story-telling is fibbing.

clue.text: One torn apart following something done by Diana, ultimately?

definitions.text: One torn apart following something done by Diana, ultimately?

indicators.note: following places one piece after the others

parts.note: an act is a deed

indicators.note: torn apart means ripped up, so the letters are scattered and put back differently
ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: its last letter
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A mythological victim ripped apart after an act committed by the goddess Diana.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: in myth the hunter who saw Diana bathing was turned into a stag by her and torn apart by his own hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Actaeon is the Greek hunter whom Diana (Artemis) transformed into a stag, after which his hounds killed him.

clue.text: Director has a hit around Southern Spain

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: scores means makes a hit, succeeds
S is the abbreviation for southern
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A film director enjoys a success across the south of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has a hit' reads as SCORES, with 'has' doing double duty as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is the American film director of Taxi Driver and Goodfellas.

clue.text: Gold given to best group, including current air traffic controller?

indicators.note: including means taking something inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
top means best
I is the physics symbol for electric current
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A medal ceremony: gold awarded to the top team, which includes a modern air traffic controller.
explanation.walkthrough: The current goes inside the two words for 'best group' together. The question mark flags that the controller is a machine flying a plane, not a person in a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopilot is a device that steers an aircraft automatically, so it controls air traffic in a whimsical sense.

clue.text: Opening temperature seen in molten iron

indicators.note: seen in places one thing inside another
molten metal has lost its shape and can be recast in any form

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
T is the standard abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A foundry note: the first temperature reading taken in melted iron.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a song or piece, a short form of introduction.

clue.text: Meal to host a debut

indicators.note: a host takes in guests, so one word holds another inside it

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lunch thrown to celebrate someone's first appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch is the first public presentation of something, the same as its debut.

clue.text: It's not always a scandal for politicians to be caught in this

definitions.text: It's not always a scandal for politicians to be caught in this

parts.words: It's not always a scandal for politicians to be caught in this
parts.note: surface reading: a political sex scandal, where politicians are caught in the act

parts.words: It's not always a scandal for politicians to be caught in this
parts.note: setter's reading: the US legislature, where politicians sit routinely without any scandal

explanation.surface: A wry remark on politicians being caught in compromising situations.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has an old sense of sexual intercourse, which suggests scandal, but it is also the name of the American legislative assembly, where being 'caught' is perfectly normal.
explanation.definitionFit: Congress is both a formal word for sexual intercourse and the national legislature of the United States, where politicians gather.

clue.text: Army shells exploded without causing damage

indicators.note: exploded means blown apart, so the letters are scattered into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Military shells blew up but nobody was hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmlessly is an adverb meaning in a way that does no injury, matching the adverbial phrase.

clue.text: A hitch, with landmass quaking in Pacific territory

indicators.note: something quaking is shaken about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A problem arises as land shakes in an earthquake somewhere in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chatham Islands are an archipelago in the South Pacific belonging to New Zealand.

clue.text: Go on with abandon at the eleventh hour

parts.note: to last is to continue, go on
to ditch is to abandon

explanation.surface: Carrying on with reckless freedom right at the final moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandon' looks like the noun (wildness) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final desperate one made at the latest possible moment, the idiomatic eleventh hour.

clue.text: Austrian composer raised concern in French commune

parts.note: Alban Berg, the Austrian composer of Wozzeck

indicators.note: raised means lifted upward, and in a down clue that runs the word from bottom to top

parts.note: care means concern

explanation.surface: A Viennese composer voiced worries while staying in a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' looks like 'voiced', but in a down clue it turns the word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Bergerac is a town and commune in the Dordogne in south-west France.

clue.text: Expression of unconcern playing cameo — yes, simple thing to play

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are toyed with and moved around

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
easy means simple
Go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: An actor shrugs off a small cameo role: yes, it's an easy part to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thing to play' looks like a role but is the game Go.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said by someone untroubled about losing what they gained without effort, a casual shrug.

clue.text: Part of cow seen with quiet frisson

parts.note: 'sh!' is a call for quiet
the udder is the cow's milk gland

explanation.surface: A cow's udder, together with silence, produces a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisson is a sudden shiver of excitement or fear, which is a shudder.

clue.text: Respectable toilet, mostly sheltered, on reflection

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the gents is a British name for a men's lavatory

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lee is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: A decent loo, largely protected from the weather, when you think about it.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage 'the gents' is a men's toilet; it loses its last letter, and LEE is read backwards after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel means polite and refined, respectable in a somewhat affected way.

clue.text: Writer's mother enthralled by Quaker leader

indicators.note: to be enthralled is to be held captive, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: William Penn, Quaker founder of Pennsylvania
ma is mother

explanation.surface: An author's mother is captivated by a Quaker leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A penman is someone who writes, especially an author or skilled calligrapher.

clue.text: Infantryman under command is pleased

parts.note: grunt is slang for an infantry soldier
led means commanded, directed

explanation.surface: A foot soldier serving under orders is content.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is a humorous back-formation from 'disgruntled'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruntled is a jocular coinage meaning satisfied, made by dropping the negative prefix from disgruntled.

clue.text: Dance beat with energy

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
go means energy, vigour

explanation.surface: A dance with an energetic rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like a musical rhythm but is the verb meaning to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Danish city, second to Copenhagen, not spread out

indicators.note: second to points to the letter in position two of the following word

parts.note: its second letter
dense means compact, closely packed

explanation.surface: A Danish city described as coming second after the capital, and compactly built.
explanation.definitionFit: Odense is the third-largest city in Denmark, on the island of Funen.

clue.text: See 4
Extracting energy, continue to study gas

indicators.note: extracting means pulling something out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: read on means keep studying
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Instructions for a student: take out the energy part and carry on studying the gas.
explanation.walkthrough: E is removed from READ ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas, element 86.

clue.text: Tense, buttonholed by more brusque male, but not for long

indicators.note: to be buttonholed is to be detained by someone, held within their grasp

parts.note: shorter means curter, more abrupt
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A nervous person is collared by a rather curt man, but only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-term means lasting only a brief period, the same as not for long.

clue.text: Vehicle repairer of the year, initially with ginger hair

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.note: opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: The garage mechanic who has won an annual award turns out to be a redhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroty describes hair of an orange-red colour like carrots, so a carroty person has ginger hair.

clue.text: Switzerland leading the Spanish in one distributed hierarchical group

indicators.note: in places the first pair of pieces inside the other
distributed means spread around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: leading puts one piece in front of the next

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Switzerland heading the Spanish in a single dispersed group arranged by rank.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland; the Swiss and Spanish pieces sit together inside the scrambled 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a level or rank in an organisation, or a group at one such level of a hierarchy.
